why: Rule 1 at the lowest-z multi-prong junction: two of the three prongs at 4005 (the 14 cm mu toward 4006 and the e toward 4001) start near zero and get hotter away, and the pi+ arm's hot patch peaks 2-3 cm before 4005 rather than at it.
Short-proton signature plus rule 1: a 3.9 cm dark-red stub at 124k e/cm hangs off 5003 at 125 deg from a 19.5 cm MIP track that cools away toward 5000, the classic proton + muon neutrino vertex.

Rule 1 on the only long measured prong: the 26.6 cm segment is 38k at 11000 and rises x2.73 to 105k at 11001, so it stops at 11001, and 11000 sits at the low-z apex of the fan of short fragments from clusters 54/57/53.

Two-Bragg-ends trap: 119k at 5001 and 193k at 5002 with the coolest point 62k at 5003, so both arms rise away from 5003; confidence dropped one tier because the two prongs leave 5003 at about 170 deg.

Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction: the prongs to 17002 and 17005 both rise away (x1.38 and x1.30) and all three prongs start cold at 17004 in the profile panel, while the 19.5 cm arm's 143k reading is a mid-track hot patch, not an end Bragg.
Rule 1 in its cleanest form: all three prongs rise away from 11003, a 72 cm proton to 177k at 11000, a 62 cm muon to 117k at 11004 and a 38 cm pion to 108k at 11002.

Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction once the chargeless grey prong toward 11002 (2-4k e/cm) is discounted as unmeasured: nothing rises toward 11003 and the 8.5 cm prong rises away, while cluster 51 reads as one smoothly stopping track (46k to 86k to 107k) rather than a vertex.

Rule 8 abstention: no junction anywhere in the event, just three disjoint blobs (a perfectly flat 60k 15 cm track at z=328, a 173k stub at z=359 and a 271k stub at z=434) with no convergence, so any click would be a guess.

Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction: no prong is hotter at 71065 and the three prongs leave at 100, 121 and 138 deg, whereas the rival 8004 is a deg-2 kink whose prongs leave at 166 deg, which the collinearity trap penalises.

Rule 1 at the only deg-3 junction of the one compact multi-prong cluster: the 7.7 cm prong rises monotonically from 15k to 72k away toward 41035 and nothing rises toward 41034, while the 317 cm and 53 cm clusters are single unbranched tracks.
Rule 1 in its cleanest form: all three prongs rise away from 6004, a 14 cm proton to 210k at 6005, a 28 cm pion to 147k at 6000 and a 42 cm muon to 99k at 6001.

Stopping-proton signature: the 5.1 cm prong reads 253k at 25010 and falls monotonically toward 25012, so 25012 is its start, and it is a deg-3 star with nothing rising toward it, while cluster 16's 132k feature is a mid-segment blob, not an end Bragg.
Rule 1 plus a textbook proton: a 10 cm dark-red arm rising to 218k at 17002 leaves 17001 at 85 deg from a 168 cm MIP muon, and 17001 is the most upstream junction in the event at z=37.

Two-Bragg-ends trap resolved at the only junction in the event: both arms are coolest at 11003 and end hot (205k at 11001, 218k at 11000), so both point away from it, and the prongs leave at 121 deg so the collinearity trap does not apply.
